subtopic: Spherical Mirrors: Reflection Ray Paths
question: Why does a ray of light passing through the center of curvature (C) of a concave mirror retrace its path back along the same line after reflection?
options: The speed of light doubles at the center of curvature
The ray strikes the spherical surface along the normal, making angle of incidence i = 0° and angle of reflection r = 0°
The mirror surface at the center of curvature is perfectly flat
Total internal reflection occurs at the focal boundary
explanation: Any line joining the center of curvature to any point on the spherical mirror is perpendicular (normal) to the reflecting surface at that point. Hence, a ray passing through C falls normally on the mirror (angle of incidence i = 0°), and by the law of reflection (r = i = 0°), it reflects straight back along the same path.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.1 Representation of Images Formed by Spherical Mirrors Using Ray Diagrams

subtopic: Convex Mirror: Numerical Image Position Calculation
question: A convex mirror used for rear-view on an automobile has a radius of curvature of 3.0 m. If a bus is located at 5.0 m in front of this mirror, what is the position and nature of the image of the bus?
explanation: Radius of curvature R = +3.0 m, so focal length f = R / 2 = +1.5 m. Object distance u = -5.0 m. Using the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/(1.5) - 1/(-5.0) = 1/1.5 + 1/5.0 = (10/15) + (3/15) = 13/15. Thus v = +15/13 ≈ +1.15 m. The positive sign indicates the image is formed behind the mirror (virtual and erect).
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Example 9.1

subtopic: Concave Mirror: Focal Length Determination from Magnification
question: A concave mirror produces a real inverted image of magnification m = -1 when an object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of it. What is the focal length of this concave mirror?
explanation: When m = -1, the object is positioned at the center of curvature (C), so the radius of curvature R = 30 cm. Focal length f = - R / 2 = - 30 / 2 = -15 cm (negative according to Cartesian sign convention for concave mirror).
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.4 Mirror Formula and Magnification

subtopic: Refraction: Direction of Bending and Wave Speed
question: When a ray of light travels obliquely from an optically denser medium into an optically rarer medium, what happens to its speed and direction?
options: Its speed decreases and it bends towards the normal
Its speed increases and it bends away from the normal
Its speed increases and it bends towards the normal
Its speed remains unchanged and it travels undeflected
explanation: In an optically rarer medium, light travels faster than in an optically denser medium. As light speeds up across the interface into the rarer medium, the wave front pivots such that the refracted ray bends away from the normal.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3 Refraction of Light

subtopic: Refraction: Normal Incidence
question: A ray of light enters normally (at angle of incidence i = 0°) from air into a flat glass slab. What is the angle of refraction (r)?
explanation: According to Snell's law, sin(i) / sin(r) = n. When the ray strikes along the normal, i = 0°, so sin(i) = 0. Therefore sin(r) = 0, giving angle of refraction r = 0°. The ray enters without any deviation in its path, though its speed decreases.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.1 Laws of Refraction of Light

subtopic: Refractive Index: Optical Density vs Mass Density
question: Turpentine oil has a refractive index of 1.47, while water has a refractive index of 1.33. However, turpentine floats on water because its mass density is lower than water. Which of the following conclusions is scientifically accurate?
options: Optical density is always directly proportional to mass density
Optical density is not the same as mass density; turpentine has higher optical density despite lower mass density
Water has a higher optical density than turpentine because it is heavier
Light travels faster in turpentine than in water
explanation: NCERT specifically highlights that optical density does not equal mass density. Turpentine oil floats on water (lower mass density), yet its refractive index (1.47) is greater than water (1.33), meaning it is optically denser than water and light travels slower in turpentine than in water.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2 Refractive Index

subtopic: Convex Lens: Needle Problem and Lens Power Calculation
question: A convex lens forms a real and inverted image of a needle at a distance of 50 cm from it. If the image is the same size as the needle, where is the needle placed in front of the lens, and what is the power of the lens?
explanation: Same size real inverted image means magnification m = -1. For a lens, m = v / u = -1, so u = -v = -50 cm. The needle is placed at 2F1, so 2f = 50 cm, meaning focal length f = +25 cm = +0.25 m. Power P = 1 / f = 1 / (+0.25 m) = +4.0 D.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, NCERT Exercise Question 16

subtopic: Concave Lens: Object Distance Calculation
question: A concave lens has a focal length of 15 cm. At what distance should an object be placed from the lens so that it forms an image at 10 cm from the lens?
explanation: For a concave lens, focal length f = -15 cm and image distance v = -10 cm (since virtual image is formed on the same side). From lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/u = 1/v - 1/f = -1/10 - (-1/15) = -1/10 + 1/15 = (-3 + 2)/30 = -1/30. Thus, u = -30 cm.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Example 9.3

subtopic: Focal Length Measurement Experiment
question: A student focuses the sharp image of a distant tree on a paper screen using a concave mirror in a laboratory experiment. What does the measured distance between the mirror and the screen represent?
options: Radius of curvature of the mirror
Approximate focal length of the mirror
Twice the focal length of the mirror
explanation: Rays coming from a distant object (like a faraway tree) are parallel to the principal axis. After reflection from a concave mirror, parallel incident rays converge at the principal focus. Hence, the distance between the mirror and the screen where the sharp image is formed equals the focal length (f).
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Activity 9.2

subtopic: Magnification: Interpretation of Signs and Values
question: In an optical experiment, the magnification calculated for an image formed by a spherical mirror is m = -0.5. What does this value tell you about the nature and size of the image?
options: Real, inverted, and diminished to half the object size
Real, inverted, and magnified by a factor of 2
explanation: The negative sign of magnification (m < 0) signifies that the image is inverted and real. The numerical magnitude |m| = 0.5 < 1 signifies that the image is diminished to half the size of the object.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.4 Mirror Formula and Magnification

subtopic: Magnification: Positive Magnification Interpretation
question: If the magnification of an image produced by an optical device is m = +1.5, which optical device could have formed this image, and what is its nature?
options: Concave mirror or Convex lens (virtual, erect, and magnified)
explanation: A positive magnification (m > 0) means the image is erect and virtual. A magnitude greater than 1 (|m| = 1.5 > 1) means the image is magnified. Neither a plane mirror (m = +1) nor a convex mirror/concave lens (always m < 1) can produce a magnified virtual image. Only a concave mirror (object between P and F) or a convex lens (object between O and F1) produces m > +1.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.4 & 9.3.7

subtopic: NCERT Exemplar: Covered Convex Lens
question: One-half of a convex lens is wrapped in opaque black paper. Will this lens still produce a complete image of an object, and what change will be observed in the image?
options: Only half the image will be formed, but with full brightness
A complete image will still be formed, but its brightness and intensity will be reduced
No image will be formed at all because symmetry is broken
The image will become virtual and inverted
explanation: Light rays from every single point of the object pass through all parts of the lens. Covering the lower (or upper) half still allows rays passing through the unblocked half to converge at the focal plane, forming a complete image. However, because half of the incoming light energy is blocked, the brightness (intensity) of the image is reduced.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, NCERT Exercise Question 9

subtopic: Refraction: Time of Light Transit
question: Light enters from vacuum into a glass sheet of thickness 2 mm (2 × 10^-3 m) and refractive index n = 1.5. If the speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10^8 m/s, how long does light take to travel perpendicularly across the glass sheet?
explanation: Speed of light in glass v = c / n = (3 × 10^8 m/s) / 1.5 = 2 × 10^8 m/s. The time taken to traverse thickness d = 2 × 10^-3 m is t = d / v = (2 × 10^-3 m) / (2 × 10^8 m/s) = 1.0 × 10^-11 s.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2 Refractive Index

subtopic: Sign Convention: Positive Focal Length Devices
question: Which group of optical devices strictly has a POSITIVE focal length (+f) under the New Cartesian Sign Convention?
explanation: Under Cartesian convention, the focus of a convex mirror lies behind the reflecting surface (to the right of the pole), and the principal focus of a convex lens lies to the right of the optical center. Hence, both convex mirrors and convex lenses have positive focal lengths (+f).
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.3 & 9.3.7

subtopic: Sign Convention: Negative Focal Length Devices
question: A student measures a negative focal length (f = -20 cm) for an optical component. Which optical component could this be?
options: Either a concave mirror or a concave lens
Either a convex mirror or a convex lens
explanation: Under Cartesian convention, the focus of both a concave mirror and a concave lens lies to the left of the optical origin (against incident light), making their focal lengths negative.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.3 & 9.3.7

subtopic: Refraction Phenomenon: Apparent Shallowing of Swimming Pools
question: The bottom of a water tank or swimming pool appears to be raised when viewed from above. This apparent depth illusion occurs due to:
options: Total internal reflection of ambient light
Refraction of light rays bending away from the normal as they emerge from water into air
Scattering of blue light by water molecules
Dispersion of light inside the water medium
explanation: Light rays originating from the tank bottom travel from optically denser water into rarer air. Upon reaching the surface, they bend away from the normal. An observer tracing these refracted rays backward sees a virtual image of the bottom at an elevated position, making the tank appear shallower.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3 Refraction of Light

subtopic: Convex Mirror: Location Range of Image
question: For any real object positioned anywhere in front of a convex mirror (between infinity and the pole), where is the image ALWAYS formed?
options: In front of the mirror between F and C
Behind the mirror between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F)
explanation: For any object placed in front of a convex mirror at a finite distance, the image is formed behind the mirror between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F). It is always virtual, erect, and diminished.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.2 Image Formation by a Convex Mirror

subtopic: Prescription Eyeglass Optics: Focal Length Calculation
question: A student with nearsightedness is prescribed a corrective lens of power P = -4.0 D. What is the focal length and nature of the prescribed lens?
explanation: Focal length f = 1 / P = 1 / (-4.0 D) = -0.25 m = -25 cm. The negative focal length indicates a concave (diverging) lens, which diverges light rays to correct myopia.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.8 Power of a Lens

subtopic: Combination of Lenses: Converging vs Diverging Behavior
question: An optical system combines two thin lenses with powers +2.5 D and -1.0 D in close contact. How does this combined lens system behave toward an incident parallel beam of light?
options: It acts as a diverging system with net power -1.5 D
It acts as a converging system with net power +1.5 D and focal length +66.7 cm
It acts as a plane glass plate with zero net power
It completely absorbs all transmitted light
explanation: Net power P = P1 + P2 = +2.5 D + (-1.0 D) = +1.5 D. Since the net power is positive, the system acts as a converging lens with focal length f = 1 / 1.5 ≈ +0.667 m = +66.7 cm.
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.8 Power of a Lens

subtopic: Medium Comparison: Optical Density Comparison Table
question: The refractive indices of four media A, B, C, and D are: nA = 1.33, nB = 1.44, nC = 1.52, and nD = 1.65. In which medium does light travel with the HIGHEST speed, and in which does it bend the MOST towards the normal when entering from air at 45°?
options: Highest speed in D; bends most in A
Highest speed in A; bends most in D
Highest speed in C; bends most in B
Speed and bending are identical in all four media
explanation: Speed of light v = c / n. Therefore, light travels fastest in the medium with the lowest refractive index (medium A with n = 1.33). Conversely, greater refractive index causes greater reduction in speed and greater bending towards the normal; hence light bends the most in medium D (n = 1.65).
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2 Refractive Index
